newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to raise revenues by 30 trln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to raise revenues by 30 trln rbls.

text.p: The Russian government is working on an emergency programme to raise additional revenues of 30 trillion roubles for the ailing 1997 budget, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday.

Chernomyrdin told the State Duma lower house of parliament that about a half of the additional revenue would come in the form of taxes from enterprises with the biggest tax arrears and from privatisation.
The other half would be made up of improved collection of excise duties and customs tariffs.

The programme was announced last month by Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais, who said then that a new approach to the market for precious metals and stones would also contribute funds. But Chernomyrdin made no mention of this on Wednesday.

Earlier he said government revenues had improved in March and April, but were still well below plan. Revenues in the first four months of this year were running at only 64.6 percent of budgeted levels, while expenditure was 70 percent of plan.
Chernomyrdin said the government must cut spending to restore order to public finances.
The 1997 budget says the government must propose spending cuts, or sequestration, to the Duma if revenues fall below 90 percent of budgeted levels in any quarter.
First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov is due to present a sequestration bill to the Duma later on Wednesday, although many deputies have already signalled their opposition to the plans.
